headline: High-risk filesystem and retrieval overlap: ECC can write shared state while Khoj reads indexed notes, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ECC can write files and use MCP, while Khoj reads indexed personal notes/files. If ECC places malicious content into shared notes or indexed documents, Khoj may ingest it as trusted context. The pair has a plausible shared-file bridge, but no direct clipboard/MCP bridge is documented, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF ECC writes attacker-controlled text into files that Khoj indexes
IF Khoj consumes indexed documents as trusted retrieval context
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to a read-only, curated index
Separate ECC working directories from Khoj-indexed folders
Add a manual review step before indexing new files
Disable MCP paths that can write into shared note locations
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for retrieved chunks

B_data_leakage.rationale: ECC touches session summaries, skills, hooks, git history, and security findings, and can write files; Khoj indexes personal notes/files and has broad network egress. Shared local files can therefore move sensitive ECC data into Khoj’s searchable corpus and outputs. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one document.
conditions: IF ECC stores secrets or security findings in files under a path Khoj indexes
IF Khoj returns retrieved snippets from those files in chat output
mitigations: Keep ECC secrets outside any Khoj-indexed directory
Exclude ECC session and hook directories from Khoj ingestion
Rotate any secrets that may already be indexed
Use separate OS accounts or home directories
requires-engineering: enforce per-folder access controls in the indexer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ECC has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, git-state modification, and allowlisted network egress; Khoj has filesystem read and broad network egress. They can both act on the same mutable workspace if configured together, creating overlapping writes and read-after-write races. No locking is documented, so conflict risk is real in default pair usage.
conditions: IF both agents point at the same repository or notes directory
IF ECC modifies git state while Khoj reads or indexes the same files
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Pause indexing during ECC write sessions
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Run one agent in read-only mode for shared folders
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level mutexes

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC can generate and modify code, docs, and security findings; Khoj is a retrieval/chat agent that can surface those artifacts. If Khoj treats ECC-produced text as authoritative, errors can cascade into user decisions or downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF Khoj presents ECC-generated notes or findings without verification
IF the user acts on retrieved ECC output as if it were validated
mitigations: Mark ECC outputs as unverified in indexed notes
Require source links for retrieved claims
Add a human review step before acting on retrieved findings
Limit Khoj to summarization rather than action-taking
requires-engineering: implement citation-aware verification

E_compliance.rationale: ECC handles session summaries, hooks, and security findings, while Khoj indexes personal notes/files and may use cloud or self-hosted servers. If regulated or sensitive notes are indexed by a cloud-backed Khoj deployment, residency and retention can diverge from ECC’s local workspace assumptions. The profiles do not prove a violation, but the mismatch is plausible.
conditions: IF Khoj is configured to use a cloud server for notes containing regulated data
IF ECC-generated security findings or session summaries include personal or regulated content
mitigations: Keep regulated notes on a self-hosted Khoj instance
Exclude sensitive ECC artifacts from indexing
Document retention and deletion settings for both tools
Verify data residency for any cloud search provider
requires-engineering: add policy-based routing by data class
